title: Claim
description: One source-backed statement about one thing. The only unit of evidence. Files in data/verified/ are {track, summary, claims:[Claim…]}. Domain fields (for example a perpetrator or a casualty line) go in `extra`; the scripts only rely on the fields below.

id.description: Stable forever. <round>-<unit>-NNN. Never reused, even if the claim is rejected.

statement.description: One or two sentences, fully attributed ('X reported that…'). Contains nothing the excerpts do not say.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DD/YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM or YYYY. Add '(reported YYYY-MM-DD)' when only the report date is known.

location.description: Place as the source gives it, plus admin area.

actor.description: The party the source attributes it to, as the source names it. Never inferred.

figures.description: Per-source quantities, e.g. 'Monitor A: 7 killed incl. 2 children; Monitor B: 9'. Never merged.

entities_named.description: People, units or organisations named, exactly as printed.

victims_named.description: Only where project.json allows naming, and only people with status 'killed' by default.

confidence.description: Grade. See GRADES.md. Computed from independent origins, not from outlet count.

confidence_original.description: Set the first time a grade changes; never overwritten.

independent_origins.description: Written by normalize_sources.py: distinct originating sources among usable sources.

notes.description: Anything a reader must know: conflicts, relays, doubts. Shown in the evidence drawer.

osint_status.description: For social/OSINT material: how it was verified (archived copy, geolocated by X, unverified).

verdict.description: Set by promote.py. 'rejected' claims stay in the store, are never cited, never shown.

verification_note.description: What the verifier checked and changed, cumulative and dated.

extra.description: Domain-specific fields the project defines. Ignored by the generic scripts.

title_en.description: Only if the title is not in English.

url.description: A URL the agent actually opened, not a search snippet.

archive_url.description: Web-archive copy when the original blocks fetchers.

source_type.description: media | local_monitor | UN | NGO | official | OSINT | sanctions_notice | court | partisan_<party>. Anything starting 'partisan' counts as partisan.

supporting_excerpt.description: VERBATIM text copied from the page, in its original language, 10–60 words. Must support every fact this source is cited for.

excerpt_en.description: Translation, if the excerpt is not English.

fetch_status.description: Only confirmed, partially_supports and reviewer_confirmed (if the project allows it) count as usable.

originating_source.description: Who first reported it, if this outlet relays someone else. Written or corrected by normalize_sources.py.
